questions.question: Compare the aromaticity in heterocycles: pyridine, pyrrole, and furan. / Comment on their basicity differences.
questions.solution_html:
• Compare the aromaticity in heterocycles: pyridine, pyrrole, and furan. Comment on their basicity
  • differences.
  • • Pyridine, pyrrole, and furan are heteroaromatic compounds
  • • Each satisfies Hückel’s 4n + 2 π-electron rule (n = 1).
  • Compound Structure Aromaticity Explanation
  • Pyridine Cyclic, Planar, fully conjugated ring with 6 π-electrons (from three C=C bonds);
  • nitrogen’s lone pair lies in an sp² orbital outside the π-system → aromatic.
  • Pyrrole Cyclic, Planar, conjugated five-membered ring with 4 π-electrons from two C=C
  • bonds; nitrogen contributes its lone pair to the π-system, making a total of 6 π
  • electrons → aromatic.
  • Furan Cyclic, Planar, conjugated five-membered ring with 4 π-electrons from two C=C
  • bonds; oxygen donates one of its lone pairs into conjugation, giving 6 π-electrons
  • → aromatic, though less so than pyrrole or pyridine due to oxygen’s high
  • electronegativity.
  • Aromatic stability order
  • Pyridine > Pyrrole > Furan (based on resonance energy and delocalization efficiency).
  • (Structure of three compounds – 1 x 3= (3 marks), Explanation on aromaticity including Hückel’s rule (Any
  • two valid points)→ 3x3=(9 marks);
  • Second part of the question is out of syllabus→ Give (2 marks) to all)
questions.final_answer: Second part of the question is out of syllabus→ Give to all)
questions.source_exam: Third Semester MGU-UGP(Hons.) Regular Exam Oct 2025
